summary: Looked at the systems behind the raise. Agreed to use the existing CRM rather than buy a specialist IR platform, a probability-weighted commitment forecast and a monthly dashboard for the partners. The DDQ answer library is pending resourcing.

discussion.keyPoints: Natalie runs LP tracking in spreadsheets. A specialist IR platform was quoted at around £25k a year. Richard prefers to use the CRM the deal team already has.
Partners have no shared view of likely commitments. Richard wants a single number each month.
Natalie rewrites the same DDQ answers each time and estimated a library of around 300 answers would cover most questions.

recommendations.recommendation: Move LP tracking into the existing deal CRM rather than buy a specialist IR platform, saving around £25k a year.
Run a weighted commitment forecast: 90% at Investment committee, 50% at Due diligence and 20% at Data room.
Present a monthly fundraising dashboard to the partners meeting with commitments, soft circles and stage counts.
Build a DDQ answer library of around 300 approved answers.

actions.action: Set up the LP pipeline in the existing CRM

nextFocus: Plan Fund III marketing and thought leadership.
nextPreparation: Bring Fund II portfolio case study material and recent press.

tests.question: Are we buying a specialist IR platform?
